editorial.title: PolinRider reached a Packagist development branch through compromised Git access
editorial.summary: Socket found malicious code in development versions of the visanduma/nova-two-factor Packagist package and traces the changes to a compromised developer account. Its report identifies no malicious stable release at the time it was written. The meaningful exposure check is whether a project resolved the affected development branch or executed compromised repository content.
editorial.why_it_matters: The campaign can move through source collaboration before a formal package release. A registry listing or cumulative download count cannot establish how many installations executed malicious code; direct branch consumers and developers opening a compromised repository need separate checks.
editorial.action: Inspect Composer constraints and lockfiles for dev-main or other affected development references, preserve repository and workstation evidence, and avoid the branch until the maintainer confirms a clean state. If suspect code executed, investigate the host and rotate accessible credentials from a trusted environment.

sections.heading: The observed Packagist scope
paragraphs: Socket reports malicious code in visanduma/nova-two-factor’s dev-main version as the PolinRider campaign expanded into Packagist. It says the malicious content was in unstable dev versions and that it had not identified a malicious stable release at publication time. This is a narrower finding than saying every installation of the package was compromised.

The research traces malicious changes to the LaHiRu developer account and says the organization’s repositories showed compromise dating back to mid-June. Private-repository contribution activity limited Socket’s ability to determine total repository reach. Those unknowns should remain open rather than becoming a campaign-wide installation estimate.

sections.heading: Source collaboration is part of the path
paragraphs: PolinRider uses compromised Git access to put payloads into normal development material. Socket documents samples that can trigger when a developer opens a repository in a compatible editor, as well as other build and test paths. That makes a checked-out repository relevant even if no stable package release was pulled.

For Packagist users, inspect whether Composer resolved a development branch and which commit it selected. For developers and maintainers, review account access, unexpected history changes and automatic execution paths in the repository. A source cleanup alone cannot establish integrity after a payload ran on a workstation.

sections.heading: Bound the response
paragraphs: Socket advises avoiding dev-main until the repository is confirmed clean. Hold the affected development dependency, compare it with a reviewed commit or stable release, and retain the resolved revision as investigation evidence.

If a host opened or built compromised source and executed a suspicious path, isolate it, investigate available credentials and rebuild from a trusted state. The original research does not establish that every stable consumer or all private repositories experienced execution or exfiltration.
